n: Oliver Cowdery wanted to translate too. The Lord promises that as surely as he lives, Oliver will gain knowledge of ancient records if he asks in faith with an honest heart.

f.w: ask in faith, with an honest heart

n: A key verse on how revelation works: God speaks to both the mind (thoughts and understanding) and the heart (feelings) through the Holy Ghost.

f.w: I will tell you in your mind and in your heart

n: This is the spirit of revelation — the same power by which Moses led Israel through the Red Sea. Even dramatic miracles were guided by quiet inspiration.

f.w: through the Red Sea on dry ground

n: Revelation is Oliver’s gift. If he uses it, it will protect him from enemies who would destroy him.

f.g: give diligent attention to it; put it to use.

n: The Lord urges Oliver to remember these words and keep the commandments, repeating: this is your gift.
Oliver has another gift, the “gift of Aaron.” Earlier versions called it a gift of working with a rod; Aaron’s rod in Exodus was a tool through which God showed his power.

f.g: The 1833 Book of Commandments called this “the gift of working with the rod.” Its exact nature is not fully known.

n: Only God’s power can make this gift work. It is not magic but divine help.
Oliver should not doubt, since the gift is from God. He will hold it in his hands and do marvelous works, and no one can take it from him.
Whatever Oliver asks to know through this means, the Lord will tell him.
Faith is essential — without it nothing can be done. Oliver must not treat sacred things lightly or ask for inappropriate things.

f.w: without faith you can do nothing

n: Oliver should ask to understand God’s mysteries and to translate sacred hidden records. It will be done according to his faith.

f.w: according to your faith shall it be done unto you

n: The Lord affirms he is the same one who has spoken to Oliver from the beginning — including the private answer recalled in D&C 6.

f.w: I am the same that spake unto you from the beginning
